canonicalFacts.claim: Endometriosis is a chronic, estrogen-dependent, inflammatory disease affecting up to 10% of women worldwide during reproductive years
90% of people with endometriosis report pelvic pain including dysmenorrhea, nonmenstrual pelvic pain, and dyspareunia, while 26% report infertility
Risk factors include younger age at menarche, shorter menstrual cycle length, lower body mass index, nulliparity, and congenital obstructive müllerian anomalies

Endometriosis-associated infertility involves complex interactions between disease subtype, pain, inflammation, altered pelvic anatomy, adhesions, disrupted ovarian function, and compromised endometrial receptivity
Currently available medications are only effective in treating endometriosis-related pain but are not targeted treatments for the underlying disease
Medical therapies provide symptom relief but are unsuitable for women wishing to conceive, while surgery may enhance natural conception but can negatively impact ovarian reserve

redFlags: Surgery for endometriosis may negatively impact ovarian reserve
Medical/hormonal treatments are unsuitable for women trying to conceive
